## 🎯 Objectives

By the end of this tutorial, you will be able to:

* add a package function that launches a Shiny app; and
* audit an app before web deployment.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

## Preparation

Install the packages used in this tutorial if you do not already have them:

```r
install.packages(c("devtools", "rsconnect", "usethis"))
```

Bring the `etc5523-wpl-share` project you used in the workshop. If you missed
the workshop, or would like a clean copy containing everything completed in
class, clone the `workshop-progress` branch:

```bash
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
git clone --branch workshop-progress --single-branch \
  https://github.com/numbats/etc5523-wpl-share.git
```

Open `wplshare.Rproj`, restart R, then install any dependencies declared by the
package:

```r
devtools::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)
```

Run the app and confirm that the number, plot and table agree when **Minimum
runs** is exactly 150 in season 2024/25:

```r
shiny::runApp("inst/app")
```

:::

::: {.callout-important}
In the workshop, we completed Steps 1--3: running the app, inspecting its
reactive graph and replacing the repeated filters with `selected_batters()`.
This tutorial continues from that point with Steps 4 and 5.
:::

## 4. Make the app launchable from the package

The repository already has the structure of an R package. Files under
`inst/app` will be installed with it.

Create `R/run_app.R`, then add a documented, exported `run_app()` function:

```r
usethis::use_r("run_app")
```

The function should:

1. locate the installed `app` directory with `system.file()`; and
2. pass that directory to `shiny::runApp()`.

Generate the documentation, install the package and test the launcher:

```r
devtools::document()
devtools::install()
wplshare::run_app()
```

Why would a path such as `/Users/name/wpl-share/inst/app` fail for another
package user?

::: {.unilur-solution}
## Package launcher

```r
#' Run the WPL batting explorer
#'
#' @return No return value; called for its side effect of launching the app.
#' @export
run_app <- function() {
  app_dir <- system.file("app", package = "wplshare")
  shiny::runApp(app_dir)
}
```

`inst/app` becomes `app` at the top level of the installed package.
`system.file()` finds that location in the active R library rather than assuming
where the source repository exists on a particular computer.
:::

## 5. Audit the web deployment

Treat the hosting service as a clean Linux computer that receives only the app
bundle. Mark each item **ready**, **not ready**, or **not applicable**:

* all required files are inside `inst/app`;
* file paths are relative and match the exact case of the file names;
* package dependencies can be detected from the app code;
* there is no `install.packages()` call in the app;
* no password, token or secret is stored in the repository;
* every possible input state produces a useful response; and
* any durable writes use storage outside the app's local filesystem.

Ask `rsconnect` what it detects:

```r
rsconnect::appDependencies("inst/app")
```

Which audit item does the current app handle least well? Make one improvement
and rerun the app.

::: {.unilur-solution}
## Audit findings

The data are bundled under `inst/app/data`, paths are relative, packages are
loaded explicitly, and the source contains no installation calls or secrets.

The empty selection is poorly communicated. `req()` prevents an error in the
leader box but leaves it blank. One possible replacement is:

```r
output$leading_batter <- renderText({
  selected <- selected_batters()

  if (nrow(selected) == 0) {
    return("No batter meets this threshold")
  }

  selected$striker[which.max(selected$runs)]
})
```

A deployed app should use a database, object store or other persistent service
for durable writes because hosted instances can restart or be replaced.
:::

## Extra practice: a clean-room handover test

Exchange repositories with a partner. Open your partner's project in a fresh R
session and test whether the package can be installed and run without relying
on their source directory or your installed copy of `wplshare`.

Create a temporary package library, install the package into it, then launch the
app from that installation:

```r
test_library <- file.path(tempdir(), "wplshare-library")
dir.create(test_library, showWarnings = FALSE)

devtools::install(lib = test_library)

library(wplshare, lib.loc = test_library)
wplshare::run_app()
```

Record any missing dependency, path assumption or unclear setup instruction.
Fix one issue, restart R and repeat the handover test.

::: {.callout-note}
Installing into `test_library` prevents your partner's package from replacing
the usual installed copy of `wplshare`. The temporary installation is removed
when R clears its temporary directory.
:::

::: {.unilur-solution}
## Expected result and troubleshooting

A successful handover has three observable results:

1. `devtools::install()` completes without an error;
2. `system.file("app", package = "wplshare")` returns a path inside the
   temporary library rather than the source project; and
3. `wplshare::run_app()` launches an app whose inputs and four outputs work.

Useful diagnoses include:

* an empty result from `system.file()` means the installed package does not
  contain the expected `app` directory, or the package name is incorrect;
* `run_app()` not being exported usually means `@export` is missing or
  `devtools::document()` has not regenerated `NAMESPACE`;
* an error about a missing package means that dependency needs to be declared
  in `DESCRIPTION` and installed; and
* a file-not-found error usually reveals an absolute path, incorrect relative
  path or mismatch in filename case.

The source repositories do not need to be identical. The test passes when a
partner can install the package and launch the app without editing paths or
moving files.
:::
